title: Module-valued sections agree on a flat connected chart
statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. For a sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $S_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], etale objects $V\to S$, $W\to X$, and a chart morphism $\varphi:W\to V\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], put $q:W\to V$ equal to its first projection. If $q$ is flat, quasi-compact, and geometrically connected, then the unit-and-restriction map $G(V)\to(p^*G)(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules.

proof.text: For an abelian sheaf on V, apply the existing flat quasi-compact connected-fibre set-sections theorem to its underlying sheaf. GeometricallyConnected supplies the required connected geometric fibres.

Use the set/abelian inverse-image and direct-image comparisons and their unit equation. Evaluate at the terminal V-object. The composite of the forgotten abelian unit with the comparison isomorphisms is the bijective set unit, so cancellation and reflection by the forgetful functor prove the abelian unit is an isomorphism.

Forget module sheaves to abelian sheaves. The existing module/abelian inverse-image comparison is the adjoint transpose of the forgotten module unit and is an isomorphism. The homEquiv unit equation expresses the forgotten module unit as the abelian unit followed by the pushforward of this comparison. Thus it is an isomorphism, and forgetting modules reflects isomorphisms.
Apply the chart-sections arrow comparison and transport isomorphism of the terminal module unit along the arrow isomorphism.
